shots.details: Wide nighttime alley. Three teenagers hang out before trouble arrives. Establish friendship, personalities, beer and geography before the story turns.
beats: 0-18: settle into positions; Teen 01 leans forward and talks with hands, Teen 02 listens and checks the alley, Teen 03 stays relaxed and deadpan.
18-36: small joke/reaction cycle; Teen 01 gets a laugh, Teen 02 reacts, Teen 03 gives a delayed look.
36-60: beer can handoff; offer -> reach -> catch -> tiny fumble -> recover. Hands and can movement sell the physical interaction.
60-72: background life continues: alley lamp hum, puddle shimmer, distant street movement.
72-83: return to casual hang; no one expects the police yet.

shots.details: The environment changes before the teenagers fully react. Police remain offscreen; light, sound and shadows create pressure.
beats: 84-96: distant siren enters while conversation continues for a moment.
96-108: first light sweep crosses brick and puddles; Teen 03 notices before the others.
108-120: Teen 03 stops moving, looks toward the alley mouth, then Teen 02 follows the gaze.
120-132: headlights grow; all three stop talking.
132-143: shared stare toward danger, followed by the first panic reaction.

shots.details: The realization becomes a coordinated but messy scramble.
beats: 144-150: freeze; nobody moves for a beat.
150-160: Teen 01 grabs for the beer first; Teen 02 reaches late; Teen 03 looks for an escape route.
160-168: shouted warning lands; heads snap toward exit.
168-180: bodies turn, feet plant, and the group commits to running.
180-215: staggered acceleration; Teen 01 leads, Teen 02 follows, Teen 03 hesitates half a beat then goes.

shots.details: A physical chase beat inside the alley. The teenagers travel toward the exit, then duck into cover and peek back.
beats: 216-240: full run with different strides and arm styles.
240-260: acceleration toward the exit; police light sweeps across them.
260-272: first teen brakes and ducks; the others pile into cover.
272-286: bodies settle behind cover; one peeks too early and ducks again.
286-299: all hold while listening, with tiny breathing and eye movements.

shots.details: The panic drops into an awkward hiding beat, then the beer becomes the problem.
beats: 300-318: heavy breathing and recovery; shoulders rise/fall.
318-332: can rattles; everyone freezes.
332-348: Teen 02 looks down and realizes the six-pack is still in hand.
348-360: Teen 01 follows the gaze; Teen 03 slowly looks at the beer.
360-371: all three look toward the bush at the alley exit.

shots.dialogue: What do we do with the beer?
shots.details: A tight comedic pause built from eye-lines and hesitation.
beats: 372-382: Teen 02 asks the question.
382-395: silence; nobody has an answer.
395-405: Teen 01 looks at Teen 03.
405-419: Teen 03 looks toward the bush; the others follow.

shots.details: The phrase is the story's trigger and title-origin joke.
beats: 420-429: Teen 01 notices the bush and points.
429-438: Teen 02 understands; Teen 03 turns toward the bush.
438-450: Teen 01 commits and says the phrase.
450-455: one beat of stunned agreement; then everybody moves.

shots.details: The group physically exits the alley before the throw. The throw is a sequence of anticipation, release, flight, impact and follow-through.
beats: 456-468: first teen launches from cover.
468-480: second and third catch up; camera follows the group rather than simply zooming.
480-492: run reaches the alley mouth; thrower plants feet and winds up.
492-505: release begins; pack leaves hand while loose cans separate.
505-520: cans rotate through the air; open can begins spilling.
520-535: impact/bounce; bush branches recoil.
535-539: teens are already fleeing away from the throw.

shots.details: The beer causes a staged transformation. The bush should move from apparently ordinary foliage to unmistakably intentional character movement.
beats: 540-555: liquid continues down leaves while teens shrink into the distance.
555-568: tiny twitch; then stillness.
568-585: second twitch becomes an irregular shudder.
585-600: foliage compresses and rebounds as if something inside is waking.
600-612: first supernatural pulse.
612-625: pulse fades; bush almost returns to normal.
625-640: stronger pulse and deliberate movement.
640-647: transformation settles into a conscious stillness before Busch rises.

shots.details: Busch's first movement establishes personality: confused, newly conscious and slightly drunk.
beats: 648-665: foliage rises slowly.
665-680: head/eyes emerge and orient.
680-692: one branch arm moves late, as though Busch discovers it.
692-704: Busch steadies himself.
704-715: eyes focus on the strange world around him.
715-719: brief confused hold.

shots.details: Busch tries to understand what just happened.
beats: 720-736: looks straight ahead, processing.
736-748: notices fleeing teens.
748-760: watches them leave; tiny head/eye follow.
760-772: attention drops toward the cans.
772-791: studies the beer and his own body, realizing something is different.
792-804: Busch looks toward the alley.
804-820: slowly turns away from the chaos.
820-839: holds the look-away longer than comfortable; tiny sway sells the joke.

shots.details: Final reaction hold, then hard title cut.
beats: 840-852: Busch returns with a small reaction.
852-864: blink and tiny sway.
864-887: hold, then hard cut to title at the end of the shot.

productionRule: The canon opening is alley-based. Each shot must contain visible acting, physical movement, environmental response or a deliberate comedic hold. The phrase IN THE BUSHES precedes the throw; the teens physically exit the alley before throwing. Transformation, wake, look-away and title remain distinct.
